variables.title: Variables
variables.code:
(setq x 10)
(defvar my-global 20 "A documentation string.")

;; Local lexical/dynamic variables
(let ((a 1)
      (b 2))
  (+ a b))
variables.notes: setq assigns values. defvar declares global variables. By default Emacs Lisp uses dynamic scope, though lexical binding can be enabled per-file.

data_types.title: Data Types
data_types.code:
42                   ; integer
3.14                 ; float
"Hello"              ; string
?A                   ; character (integer)
'symbol              ; symbol
'(1 2 3)             ; list
[1 2 3]              ; vector
t                    ; true
nil                  ; false / empty list
data_types.notes: Elisp shares many types with Common Lisp. Characters are just integers. Vectors are written with square brackets.

operators.title: Operators
operators.code:
(+ 1 2 3)    ; => 6
(- 10 4)     ; => 6
(* 2 3)      ; => 6
(/ 10 2)     ; => 5

(= 1 1)      ; Numeric equality
(equal "a" "a") ; Structural equality
(eq 'a 'a)   ; Identity equality

(and t nil)  ; => nil
(or nil t)   ; => t
(not t)      ; => nil
operators.notes: Standard Lisp prefix operators. eq checks identity, equal checks structure, string= specifically compares strings.

conditionals.title: Conditionals
conditionals.notes: if, when, unless, and cond are the primary conditional constructs.

for_loop.title: For Loop
for_loop.code:
(dotimes (i 10)
  (message "Iteration %d" i))

(dolist (item '(a b c))
  (message "Item: %s" item))

(require 'cl-lib)
(cl-loop for i from 1 to 10
         collect (* i i))
for_loop.notes: dotimes and dolist are built-in for simple iterations. For more complex loops, cl-loop (from cl-lib) provides Common Lisp's loop macro.

while_loop.title: While Loop
while_loop.code:
(setq x 0)
(while (< x 10)
  (message "Value: %d" x)
  (setq x (1+ x)))

;; catch/throw can break out of loops
(catch 'break
  (while t
    (if (some-condition) (throw 'break t))))
while_loop.notes: while is the fundamental loop in Emacs Lisp. catch and throw are used for early exits, similar to break in other languages.

functions.title: Functions
functions.code:
(defun my-add (a b)
  "Add A and B together."
  (+ a b))

;; Interactive function (Command)
(defun hello-world ()
  "Print a greeting."
  (interactive)
  (message "Hello, World!"))

;; Lambda
(mapcar (lambda (x) (* x x)) '(1 2 3))
functions.notes: defun creates functions. Adding (interactive) makes the function callable via M-x. Documentation strings are built into the definition syntax.

arrays.title: Arrays (Vectors)
arrays.code:
;; Creating a vector
(make-vector 5 0)
[1 2 3 4 5] ; Literal syntax

;; Accessing and modifying
(setq v (vector 10 20 30))
(aref v 0)       ; => 10
(aset v 0 42)    ; Mutates vector
arrays.notes: Vectors are fixed-length arrays. aref gets an element, aset sets an element. Strings and bool-vectors are also array types.

maps.title: Maps (Hash Tables / Alists)
maps.code:
;; Association List (Alist)
(setq alist '((a . 1) (b . 2)))
(cdr (assoc 'a alist)) ; => 1

;; Hash Table
(setq ht (make-hash-table :test 'equal))
(puthash "key" "value" ht)
(gethash "key" ht)
(remhash "key" ht)
maps.notes: Alists (lists of cons cells) are traditionally used for small maps. Hash tables provide better performance for larger datasets.

error_handling.title: Error Handling
error_handling.code:
(condition-case err
    (/ 1 0)
  (arith-error (message "Math error: %s" err) 0)
  (error (message "Unknown error: %s" err) nil))

;; Signaling an error
(error "Something went wrong")
error_handling.notes: condition-case is the try-catch equivalent, intercepting specific error symbols. ignore-errors is a useful macro to suppress all errors.

comments.title: Comments & Annotations
comments.code:
;; Single-line comment in Lisp
#|
 Multi-line block comment
|#
(defun add (a b)
  "Documentation string for function"
  (+ a b))
comments.notes: Emacs Lisp uses functional comment delimiters (-- in Haskell/ML, ; in Lisps, # or % in BEAM).

numbers.title: Numbers & Numerics
numbers.code:
(def x 42)          ; Integer
(def pi 3.14159)    ; Float
(def ratio 1/3)     ; Exact rational ratio
(def hex #xFF)      ; Hexadecimal
numbers.notes: Emacs Lisp supports exact rational fractions, arbitrary-precision integers, and IEEE floats natively.

booleans.title: Booleans & Logic
booleans.notes: Emacs Lisp treats booleans as first-class algebraic constructors (True/False, true/false, t/nil).

type_casting.title: Type Conversion
type_casting.notes: Emacs Lisp performs conversion via typeclass methods (fromIntegral, show, read) or explicit parse functions.

strings.title: Strings & Text
strings.code:
(def s "Hello, World!")
(def char-val (char s 0))
(def multi "Line 1
Line 2")
strings.notes: Emacs Lisp represents strings as linked lists of characters, UTF-8 binaries, or dedicated text buffers.

string_formatting.title: String Formatting
string_formatting.notes: Emacs Lisp formats text through format strings, interpolation macros, or string concatenation.

pattern_matching.title: Pattern Matching
pattern_matching.notes: Pattern matching is a core feature in Emacs Lisp, destructuring algebraic variants, tuples, and lists directly.

range.title: Ranges & Sequences
range.notes: Emacs Lisp constructs ranges as lazy lists, infinite streams, or structured range enumerables.

iterators.title: Iterators & Comprehensions
iterators.notes: Emacs Lisp achieves iterative processing through list comprehensions, map/filter transforms, and recursion.

oop_classes.title: Types & Abstractions (OOP Equivalent)
oop_classes.notes: Emacs Lisp emphasizes algebraic data types, protocols/typeclasses, and structs over traditional class hierarchies.

lists.title: Lists (Linked Lists)
lists.notes: Lists in Emacs Lisp are singly linked immutable sequences optimized for head/tail structural sharing.

tuples.title: Tuples & Records
tuples.notes: Emacs Lisp uses fixed-length heterogeneous tuples for bundling related data points and function return values.

sets.title: Sets
sets.notes: Emacs Lisp provides persistent immutable sets implemented via balanced binary trees (HAMT / AVL).

modules_import.title: Modules & Imports
modules_import.notes: Emacs Lisp isolates scopes through modules and explicit import lists with aliasing and qualified names.
